entity_title: Friendly Nations visa now starts as a 2-year provisional permit
fact_text: Since Executive Decree 226 of 20 July 2021, a national of a specific/'friendly' country applying for residence under this category first receives a Provisional Resident permit valid for two (2) years, and only afterward may apply for Permanent Residence. It no longer confers immediate permanent residency as it did before the 2021 reform.
evidence_quote: El Servicio Nacional de Migración podrá conceder un permiso de Residencia Provisional por periodo de dos (2) años a aquellas personas que soliciten la subcategoría de Residente Permanente, en calidad de extranjeros nacionales de países específicos

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Pre-2021 the Friendly Nations visa granted immediate permanent residence; Decreto Ejecutivo 226 de 2021 split it into a 2-year provisional permit followed by permanent residence - a change most HR generalists and older guides still miss.

entity_title: Employment-based residence requires the MITRADEL work-permit filing
fact_text: For the employment-based specific-countries residence application, the Servicio Nacional de Migracion requires a copy of the work-permit application already filed before MITRADEL (the labour ministry). The immigration residence permit and the MITRADEL work permit are two separate procedures at two different agencies, and the employee needs both.
evidence_quote: Copia del poder y solicitud del permiso presentado ante MITRADEL firmado por el representante legal y solicitante.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Residence (Migracion) and the right to work (MITRADEL) are separate tracks; the residence packet itself demands proof that the MITRADEL work-permit request has been filed. A visa alone never authorises employment.

fact_text: To convert the 2-year provisional permit into Permanent Residence under the specific-countries category, the applicant re-submits the same documents with the exception of the Criminal Record Certificate and the certified check.
evidence_quote: Para solicitar la permanencia se presentarán los requisitos anteriores con excepción del Certificado de Antecedentes Penales y el Cheque.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The permanent-residence step reuses the provisional documents but explicitly drops the criminal-record certificate and the government check - a detail that changes what must be re-gathered from abroad at renewal.

entity_title: Two certified checks due at the provisional-permit filing
fact_text: The provisional specific-countries residence application requires two separate certified checks: B/.250.00 payable to the National Treasury (Tesoro Nacional) and B/.800.00 payable to the National Migration Service (Servicio Nacional de Migracion). The balboa is at par with, and circulates alongside, the US dollar.
evidence_quote: Cheque Certificado por B/.250.00 a favor del Tesoro Nacional.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Filing needs two distinct certified checks with different payees - B/.250 to the Treasury and B/.800 to Migracion - and these government charges are separate from legal/professional fees.

entity_title: Income threshold to add dependents to the permit
fact_text: To include dependents on the residence permit, the resident must evidence minimum income of one thousand balboas (B/.1,000.00) per month plus an additional one hundred balboas (B/.100.00) for each dependent.
evidence_quote: cumplir con el ingreso mínimo de mil balboas (B/.1,000.00) mensuales más cien balboas (B/.100.00), adicionales por cada dependiente.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Adding a spouse or children requires the principal to show B/.1,000/month plus B/.100 per dependent - a concrete financial bar HR must plan for when relocating families, not just the main applicant.

entity_title: Labour Code caps foreign staff at 15% specialists / 90% national ordinary
fact_text: Panama's Labour Code (art. 17) requires every employer to keep at least 90% of its ordinary workforce as Panamanians (or foreigners married to a Panamanian or with ten years' residence), and permits foreign specialist or technical staff only up to 15% of total workers.
evidence_quote: Todo empleador mantendrá trabajadores panameños, o extranjeros de cónyuge panameño o con diez años de residencia en el país, en proporción no inferior al 90 por ciento del personal de trabajadores ordinarios, y podrá mantener personal extranjero especializado o técnico que no exceda del 15 por ciento del total de los trabajadores.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: A hire can be blocked by the employer's headcount ratios rather than the individual's profile: the 90% national / 15% foreign-specialist caps (commonly summarised as '10%/15%') are per-employer and gate every work-permit approval.

entity_title: Employer must obtain a separate MITRADEL work authorization
fact_text: Before employing a foreigner, the employer must obtain a work authorization issued by the Ministry of Labour (MITRADEL), granted only after verifying that the required national-worker percentages are not breached. This is separate from, and additional to, the immigration residence permit.
evidence_quote: Los empleadores que necesiten ocupar trabajadores extranjeros obtendrán una autorización que expedirá el Ministerio de Trabajo y Bienestar Social, previa comprobación de que no se alteran los porcentajes de nacionales exigidos en este artículo

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The work authorization is a MITRADEL act distinct from the Migracion visa; the residence permit alone never confers the right to work, and the authorization hinges on the employer's national/foreign headcount ratios.

entity_title: MITRADEL work-permit carné expires in 3 months to 1 year
fact_text: Once MITRADEL approves a work permit, the foreigner is issued a carné (work-permit ID card) carrying an expiry of between three months and one year depending on the permit type; the 10%/15%-of-company category is issued a one-year carné.
evidence_quote: Todo extranjero que cumpla con los requisitos que exige la ley panameña para tramitar permisos de trabajo, se le otorgará su respectivo permiso y un carné con fecha de vencimiento de tres meses a un año, según el tipo de servicio.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The MITRADEL carné is the ID proving the right to work and expires within 3-12 months (one year for the 10%/15% category), so it must be renewed on a far shorter cycle than the residence permit.

entity_title: Mandatory CSS enrolment within 6 business days of hire
fact_text: All workers, national or foreign, providing services in Panama must be affiliated to the Caja de Seguro Social (CSS); under art. 77 of Law 51 of 27 December 2005 the employer must enrol the employee within the first six (6) business days from the start date.
evidence_quote: Todos los trabajadores nacionales o extranjeros que brinden servicio dentro de la República de Panamá, están obligados afiliarse al régimen de la Caja de Seguro Social, conforme lo dispone el artículo 77 de la Ley 51 de 27 de diciembre de 2005, deben ser afiliado por su empleador dentro de los primeros seis (6) días hábiles, contados a partir de su ingreso

applies_to.non_obvious_note: CSS enrolment is compulsory for foreign employees on a Panama payroll and carries a tight 6-business-day employer deadline from day one - a payroll/onboarding obligation distinct from the immigration and work-permit tracks.

entity_title: Foreign-source income is excluded from taxable income
fact_text: Panama taxes income on a territorial basis: under art. 695 of the Fiscal Code (as amended by Law 8 of 2010), taxable income is gross income less foreign-source income, exempt/non-taxable income, and deductible costs - so income from foreign sources is outside Panamanian income tax.
evidence_quote: Renta gravable del contribuyente es la diferencia o saldo que resulta al deducir de su renta bruta o ingresos generales los ingresos de fuente extranjera, los ingresos exentos y/o no gravables, así como los costos, gastos y erogaciones deducibles.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: The territorial system explicitly subtracts foreign-source income from the taxable base, so an assignee's non-Panamanian income is not taxed in Panama - a genuine draw, but only Panama-source income (e.g. the local salary) is taxable.

entity_title: Single-salary employees need not file an annual tax return
fact_text: An employee who earns a single salary is not required to file the annual income-tax return, provided the employer has withheld the full tax due under the Fiscal Code. Payroll withholding (retencion) discharges the annual filing obligation for straightforward salaried employees.
evidence_quote: No están obligados a presentar la declaración jurada anual: El trabajo que devenga un solo salario, siempre que el empleador haya retenido la totalidad del impuesto conforme a las normas del Código Fiscal y de este decreto.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: A salaried assignee with a single employer generally files no annual Panamanian return because employer withholding settles the tax - but this breaks the moment a second income source appears, which HR should flag to the employee.
